items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: You have to look at Bill Johnson... [INTERVIEWEE] Mmm-hmm.

ctx.x: Those are the ones that migrated to Chicago, migrated from New Orleans around 1915, '16 and '17, and migrated from Chicago to Frisco and Oakland and San Diego. Jelly Roll and all of them went out there, when Watts was... They speak of Watts as a cowboy place, a country...you know, Western town.
That almost makes me the oldest one now standing. After you get past Garland and Pops Foster. I guess you ...(?)... and your day will come. There it is. You have to look at Bill Johnson...

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Now you come there and you fool around, and I’ll show you the different keys.

ctx.x: Luis Russell’s man. Yeah, Bill, that’s who. I can’t think of his last name. He had a guitar, two guitars on a stand when I saw him. So he say, “Go ask him to loan you a guitar.” Your uncle’s in the band. He knows you. You ain’t going to run away with the guitar. So I went to see him, and he loaned me the guitar. He told me, he said, “You see the first four strings on that guitar. It’s the same as the ukulele. Now you come there and you fool around, and I’ll show you the different keys.” He showed me the C chord,…
Who taught you lessons when you took them?
